findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Insepctor observed an employee fail to remove gloves and hand wash prior to changing tasks on the prep line. Staff were observed wearing gloves to handle the register and immediately return to the prep line to handle food. Gloves must be removed prior to handling the cash register. Staff then must wash their hands thoroughly prior to donning new gloves. This practice needs to be completed every time staff change tasks during food service. Education was conducted during today’s visit.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed two staff members on site that did not have a valid food handler’s certification. The PIC is aware of the issue. Qdoba has recently changed policy to pay for food handler’s certification for staff. Ensure all employees have food handler’s certification prior to the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

The right corner of the sink is not graded correctly, resulting in water collecting near the wall and pouring down the wall to the floor. This area is heavily soiled. Ensure the sink is cleaned, sanitized, and repaired prior to the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels available for use at men’s restroom hand sink. Paper towels were provided at men’s restroom hand sink during inspection. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed tongs used at grill to be stored on handle of oven. Tongs were removed and placed at 3 compartment sink during inspection.

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 
None of the employees present at the time of inspection are manager certified. Provide certified managers as soon as possible. The facility shall be under working supervision of a Certified Food Protection Manager at all times.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 
Upon arrival the facility was beginning to deal with a hot holding table that had run out of water. They said that they could smell it burning and I observed an employee adding water to the unit. Chicken, white rice, pinto beans, fajita veggies, ground beef, steak, and adobo chicken are observed to be on the hot holding table at temperatures between 112 &142. Ground beef, brown rice, adobo chicken, and  fajita veggies were all discarded. There were small amounts of each one. Steak at 120, chicken at 117, were placed into the steam ovens for reheating. Black beans were placed in a pot on the stove top and reheated. The foods had been on the hot holding table for less than 2 hours according to management. Foods that were not discarded were reheated to 165.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.comment:
2-303.11: Except for a plain ring such as a wedding band, while preparing FOOD, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not wear jewelry including medical information jewelry on their arms and hands.
Observed employees with bracelets and rings on their hands and wrists. Remove bracelets and extra (non wedding) jewelry so that hand washing can be effective and so that bracelets do not come into contact with food. Maintain violation corrected.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 
The area around the three part sink is observed to have brackets attached to the wall that are rusting and no longer cleanable. Also the caulk lines at the three part sink and the left of the hood vent are soiled and need replaced. Maintain these surfaces so that they are easily cleanable.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. 
All employees not manager certified shall be handler certified within 30 days of hire. Facility states that they use ServSafe to certify employees. Keep certifications in a file available for inspector. Suggest doing this as a part of onboarding new employees.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Every certified food protection manager shall have allergen awareness training as well. Keep these certificates available and provide to inspector upon request.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
